Routine veterinary visits and diagnostic bloodwork are key elements in catching cancer early, but you can recognize the signs, too. If you notice any of these symptoms, schedule an appointment with us as soon as possible:

  * Abnormal swellings
  * Sores that don’t heal
  * Weight loss/loss of appetite
  * Lethargy or hesitation to exercise
  * Difficulty breathing, urinating or defecating
  * Bleeding from any bodily orifice
  * Unpleasant odor that won’t go away
  * Difficulty eating or swallowing


## Common Cancers in Pets

Pets can develop many of the same cancers that we can. Some of the most common include:

## Common cancers in dogs:

  * Mast cell tumors – a type of skin cancer
  * Melanoma – another type of skin cancer that is often benign
  * Lymphoma – a type of blood cell cancer
  * Bone cancer (osteosarcoma) – the most common bone tumor; often found in larger breed dogs
  * Hemangiosarcoma – a type of highly malignant cancer that causes tumors all over the body

## Common cancers in cats:

  * Lymphoma – a type of blood cell cancer
  * Squamous cell carcinoma – a type of skin cancer, often present on the ears, nose, and eyelids
  * Fibrosarcoma – an aggressive tumor that develops from fibrous connective tissue.


## Our Dog and Cat Cancer Treatments: Chemotherapy & Surgery

Advances in veterinary medicine have allowed us to more effectively treat cancer in cats and dogs so they can enjoy a good quality of life during and after treatment. At Lincolnway, we use both chemotherapy and cancer surgery to treat various forms of cancer. We also work closely with veterinary oncology specialists at our area’s universities to facilitate advanced treatment for pets who need it. This allows our clients to get local treatment rather than going further out to a specialist facility.

# IU Health Frankfort now offering chemotherapy

### January 09, 2024

Residents of Clinton County and surrounding communities now have a new option, closer to home, for receiving this important care.

Frankfort, Ind. – Indiana University Health Frankfort Hospital now offers chemotherapy services, giving area residents another option for receiving this lifesaving care without the drive.

“At a time when other healthcare organizations are reducing their presence in smaller communities, we are thrilled to offer another important service to the residents of Clinton County and surrounding communities, close to home,” says Mary Minier, chief operating officer for IU Health Frankfort and White Memorial. “Chemotherapy can be a physically and emotionally draining process. Being able to access this treatment closer to home will, we hope, make the process just a little bit easier for patients and their loved ones.”

With the addition of chemotherapy, patients now have access to a full range of infusion therapy for cancer and non-cancerous conditions in Frankfort at IU Health Frankfort Hospital on Jackson Street. To transfer infusion appointments to Frankfort, patients can call the IU Health Infusion Therapy team at 765.838.6885.

What is infusion therapy?

Infusion therapy is a method of delivering a variety of medications via IV or catheter for cancer and non-cancerous conditions, such as:

  * Autoimmune disorders
  * Blood disorders
  * Cancer
  * Electrolyte imbalances
  * Infectious diseases
  * Inflammatory conditions
  * Crohn's disease
  * Migraines or chronic headaches
  * Neurological disorders
  * Osteoporosis
  * Anemia
  * Rheumatoid Arthritis

Medications delivered via infusion can include chemotherapy, antibiotics, IV fluids, blood transfusions and more. Treatments can be one-time or ongoing and last anywhere from one to eight hours.
